#### Campaign website
Cantwell-Copher's campaign website stated the following:
# Vision
My vision for education in Fresno County prioritizes ALL children, especially those who need us most, by ensuring equal access to resources and caring adults that support a healthy development and safeguard their success for school, and for life.
# Goals
- Strengthen Public Education: Advocate for public education as a shared community responsibility essential to the future of our children and our county.
- Support Parents: Champion parents as essential partners in their child’s educational journey, beginning with strong early learning opportunities.
- Collaborate with Districts: work side-by-side with school districts, respecting and responding to their unique needs and strengths, focused on improved student outcomes.
- Drive Academic Excellence: Support school districts in achieving positive outcomes in literacy, mathematics, and high school graduation rates.
- Provide Essential Services: Continue delivering high-quality programs, services, and fiscal oversight that strengthen school district operations and student achievement.
- Promote Data-Driven Improvement: Foster a culture of data-informed decision-making and continuous improvement for students, educators, and all educational partners.
- Uplift Educators and Staff: Celebrate and support the dedicated teachers and school staff who form the village raising our children, and renew pride in the noble gift of teaching.
- Advance Opportunities: Advocate for systemic change to eliminate barriers to student success and ensure every student has the opportunity to thrive.
# Core Beliefs
- Ensuring the success of all children, especially those who need us most, is a moral imperative.
- Every student deserves the opportunity to achieve academic and personal success, and every adult shares the responsibility to nurture, support, and educate them toward that goal.
- All students have the right to high-quality teaching, safe and supportive schools, and access and opportunity.
- We value diversity in all its forms, recognizing that it enriches and strengthens our communities.
- Our schools should be fiscally responsible and deliver on promises- our public and our students deserve that.
— Michele Cantwell-Copher's campaign website (May 10, 2026)
Note: This text is quoted verbatim from the original source. Any inconsistencies are attributable to the original source.

## Campaign themes

#### Campaign website
Cantwell-Copher's campaign website stated the following:
# Vision
My vision for education in Fresno County prioritizes ALL children, especially those who need us most, by ensuring equal access to resources and caring adults that support a healthy development and safeguard their success for school, and for life.
# Goals
- Strengthen Public Education: Advocate for public education as a shared community responsibility essential to the future of our children and our county.
- Support Parents: Champion parents as essential partners in their child’s educational journey, beginning with strong early learning opportunities.
- Collaborate with Districts: work side-by-side with school districts, respecting and responding to their unique needs and strengths, focused on improved student outcomes.
- Drive Academic Excellence: Support school districts in achieving positive outcomes in literacy, mathematics, and high school graduation rates.
- Provide Essential Services: Continue delivering high-quality programs, services, and fiscal oversight that strengthen school district operations and student achievement.
- Promote Data-Driven Improvement: Foster a culture of data-informed decision-making and continuous improvement for students, educators, and all educational partners.
- Uplift Educators and Staff: Celebrate and support the dedicated teachers and school staff who form the village raising our children, and renew pride in the noble gift of teaching.
- Advance Opportunities: Advocate for systemic change to eliminate barriers to student success and ensure every student has the opportunity to thrive.
# Core Beliefs
- Ensuring the success of all children, especially those who need us most, is a moral imperative.
- Every student deserves the opportunity to achieve academic and personal success, and every adult shares the responsibility to nurture, support, and educate them toward that goal.
- All students have the right to high-quality teaching, safe and supportive schools, and access and opportunity.
- We value diversity in all its forms, recognizing that it enriches and strengthens our communities.
- Our schools should be fiscally responsible and deliver on promises- our public and our students deserve that.
— Michele Cantwell-Copher's campaign website (May 10, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Cantwell-Copher's campaign website stated the following:
# Vision
My vision for education in Fresno County prioritizes ALL children, especially those who need us most, by ensuring equal access to resources and caring adults that support a healthy development and safeguard their success for school, and for life.
# Goals
- Strengthen Public Education: Advocate for public education as a shared community responsibility essential to the future of our children and our county.
- Support Parents: Champion parents as essential partners in their child’s educational journey, beginning with strong early learning opportunities.
- Collaborate with Districts: work side-by-side with school districts, respecting and responding to their unique needs and strengths, focused on improved student outcomes.
- Drive Academic Excellence: Support school districts in achieving positive outcomes in literacy, mathematics, and high school graduation rates.
- Provide Essential Services: Continue delivering high-quality programs, services, and fiscal oversight that strengthen school district operations and student achievement.
- Promote Data-Driven Improvement: Foster a culture of data-informed decision-making and continuous improvement for students, educators, and all educational partners.
- Uplift Educators and Staff: Celebrate and support the dedicated teachers and school staff who form the village raising our children, and renew pride in the noble gift of teaching.
- Advance Opportunities: Advocate for systemic change to eliminate barriers to student success and ensure every student has the opportunity to thrive.
# Core Beliefs
- Ensuring the success of all children, especially those who need us most, is a moral imperative.
- Every student deserves the opportunity to achieve academic and personal success, and every adult shares the responsibility to nurture, support, and educate them toward that goal.
- All students have the right to high-quality teaching, safe and supportive schools, and access and opportunity.
- We value diversity in all its forms, recognizing that it enriches and strengthens our communities.
- Our schools should be fiscally responsible and deliver on promises- our public and our students deserve that.
— Michele Cantwell-Copher's campaign website (May 10, 2026)

#### Campaign website
O'Brien's campaign website stated the following:
# As your next Superintendent of Schools, I intend to prioritize the following 3 GOALS:
## GOAL #1: 3rd Grade Literacy
FACT: In Fresno County, 60% of third graders on average are not meeting reading standards. That means that in a class of 25 students, 15 are not meeting literacy standards.
Why Reading Matters
Reading is not merely a skill—it is the foundation upon which all other academic competencies are built, including mathematical reasoning, scientific inquiry, and critical thinking. By empowering students to have strong literacy skills from an early age, we will pave the way for success in every academic discipline and prepare them to navigate the complexities of the modern world.
​
How reading confidence affects our students
A focus on reading will not only elevate our county’s literacy rates but it will also allow us to tackle a variety of interconnected challenges faced by students.
- When our children acquire strong reading skills, it will nurture their self-esteem and confidence, providing them with the tools to express themselves effectively and navigate their academic journeys with assurance.
- Furthermore, by improving literacy, we can alleviate anxiety and frustration often stemming from academic struggles, fostering a more positive school environment.
- Equipped with better reading proficiency, our students will more likely engage in classroom activities, exhibit better behavior, and form stronger connections with peers and teachers.
My response
As part of my educational agenda, I will develop a comprehensive multi-year literacy plan in collaboration with our educational team to address this priority effectively. I am witnessing an exciting return to the “Back to Basics” science of reading approach that I successfully used for twenty years in my own classrooms. I hope to champion this and other proven methods in the development of our county's plan to achieve significant results for the students in our schools.
​
With this plan, we will be taking a foundational step toward enabling Fresno County’s youth to flourish both academically and personally.
## GOAL #2: Partner with Parents and Families!
Why is this important in education?
Parents play an essential role as the first and primary educators in their children's critical early years. As a parent myself, I appreciated having access to information that helped me support my children at school. At the same time, as a teacher and administrator, I saw the impact of strong school to home relationships. In short, our students achieve higher outcomes when they are supported by school and family communities sharing a common vision.
What I know works…
- Providing parents with the necessary support and knowledge around early childhood educational milestones
- Engaging parents in opportunities to learn how to help their children navigate social, emotional and academic challenges as they matriculate through the system
- Partnering with local parenting groups such as Fresno State's Parent University to create modules focused on topics of interest
- Fostering relationships with local community groups to help support family to school connections
What’s my plan?
I aim to collaborate with District leaders and community organizations specializing in parent engagement programs to help parents actively engage in their children's education. ​
​
If we partner with parents and families to support their children, we will be able to strengthen the bridge between home and school, ensuring a more cohesive and collaborative approach to education.
## GOAL #3: Let's Increase our Return on Investment in Education
What I know…
Fresno County receives significant federal and state dollars for TK-12 education totaling in the billions. Yet, our students continue to struggle, with 56% not meeting standards in English Language Arts and 68% not meeting standards in Math in 2023-24.
Why is this?
Simply put, our current approach isn’t working. My experiences in both Clovis and Central Unified have taught me that we must have the courage to change course when our students are not achieving the results they deserve.
​
The answer?
There are teachers all over our county whose students are achieving great results! We need to work together to collaborate on systems and programs that are yielding positive outcomes on a consistent basis. Only through listening to each other, supporting our teachers, and identifying the most effective programs and methodologies, will we begin to move the needle on student achievement.
​
Therefore in Fresno County, I aim to work alongside districts to explore proven approaches so that our significant investment in education returns the results we all need for our kids.
— Eimear O'Brien's campaign website (May 12, 2026)

#### Campaign website
O'Brien's campaign website stated the following:
# As your next Superintendent of Schools, I intend to prioritize the following 3 GOALS:
## GOAL #1: 3rd Grade Literacy
FACT: In Fresno County, 60% of third graders on average are not meeting reading standards. That means that in a class of 25 students, 15 are not meeting literacy standards.
Why Reading Matters
Reading is not merely a skill—it is the foundation upon which all other academic competencies are built, including mathematical reasoning, scientific inquiry, and critical thinking. By empowering students to have strong literacy skills from an early age, we will pave the way for success in every academic discipline and prepare them to navigate the complexities of the modern world.
​
How reading confidence affects our students
A focus on reading will not only elevate our county’s literacy rates but it will also allow us to tackle a variety of interconnected challenges faced by students.
- When our children acquire strong reading skills, it will nurture their self-esteem and confidence, providing them with the tools to express themselves effectively and navigate their academic journeys with assurance.
- Furthermore, by improving literacy, we can alleviate anxiety and frustration often stemming from academic struggles, fostering a more positive school environment.
- Equipped with better reading proficiency, our students will more likely engage in classroom activities, exhibit better behavior, and form stronger connections with peers and teachers.
My response
As part of my educational agenda, I will develop a comprehensive multi-year literacy plan in collaboration with our educational team to address this priority effectively. I am witnessing an exciting return to the “Back to Basics” science of reading approach that I successfully used for twenty years in my own classrooms. I hope to champion this and other proven methods in the development of our county's plan to achieve significant results for the students in our schools.
​
With this plan, we will be taking a foundational step toward enabling Fresno County’s youth to flourish both academically and personally.
## GOAL #2: Partner with Parents and Families!
Why is this important in education?
Parents play an essential role as the first and primary educators in their children's critical early years. As a parent myself, I appreciated having access to information that helped me support my children at school. At the same time, as a teacher and administrator, I saw the impact of strong school to home relationships. In short, our students achieve higher outcomes when they are supported by school and family communities sharing a common vision.
What I know works…
- Providing parents with the necessary support and knowledge around early childhood educational milestones
- Engaging parents in opportunities to learn how to help their children navigate social, emotional and academic challenges as they matriculate through the system
- Partnering with local parenting groups such as Fresno State's Parent University to create modules focused on topics of interest
- Fostering relationships with local community groups to help support family to school connections
What’s my plan?
I aim to collaborate with District leaders and community organizations specializing in parent engagement programs to help parents actively engage in their children's education. ​
​
If we partner with parents and families to support their children, we will be able to strengthen the bridge between home and school, ensuring a more cohesive and collaborative approach to education.
## GOAL #3: Let's Increase our Return on Investment in Education
What I know…
Fresno County receives significant federal and state dollars for TK-12 education totaling in the billions. Yet, our students continue to struggle, with 56% not meeting standards in English Language Arts and 68% not meeting standards in Math in 2023-24.
Why is this?
Simply put, our current approach isn’t working. My experiences in both Clovis and Central Unified have taught me that we must have the courage to change course when our students are not achieving the results they deserve.
​
The answer?
There are teachers all over our county whose students are achieving great results! We need to work together to collaborate on systems and programs that are yielding positive outcomes on a consistent basis. Only through listening to each other, supporting our teachers, and identifying the most effective programs and methodologies, will we begin to move the needle on student achievement.
​
Therefore in Fresno County, I aim to work alongside districts to explore proven approaches so that our significant investment in education returns the results we all need for our kids.
— Eimear O'Brien's campaign website (May 12, 2026)

### On the Board of Supervisors, MIKE KARBASSI will...
### KEEP FRESNO COUNTY COMMUNITIES SAFE
On the Fresno City Council, Mike Karbassi fought to deliver a historic 900 police officers and 300 firefighters to the force. As our Supervisor, he’ll continue his pledge to only vote for budgets that maintain or add public safety personnel to reduce response times and keep our communities safe.
### CONTINUE TO REDUCE HOMELESSNESS IN OUR COMMUNITIES
Mike Karbassi led the charge to clean up Fresno’s streets and worked to reduce homelessness by more than 25 percent since taking office in 2019. On the Board of Supervisors, he’ll continue to deploy more resources to the westside to get the homeless off our streets and into housing and treatment.
### INVEST IN OUR NEIGHBORHOODS
Mike Karbassi believes that no neighborhood should be left behind. That’s why he’s committed to building new workforce and affordable housing, combating illegal roadside dumping, improving roads, delivering safe routes to schools and investing in parks and trails.
### BE THE VOICE OF THE WESTSIDE ON THE BOARD
The best leaders are ones who listen. As our Supervisor, Mike will listen and fight to strengthen the communities of western Fresno County.
I have a proven record of delivering safe, vibrant neighborhoods, safer roads, combating illegal street racing, lowering the cost of housing for Fresno County residents, increasing park space, and reducing homelessness.
On the Board of Supervisors, I will be your voice and champion for safe, family-friendly communities on the westside. I’d be honored to have your vote!

Mike Karbassi is a member of the Fresno City Council in California, representing District 2. He assumed office in 2019. His current term ends on January 2, 2029.
Karbassi ran for election to the Fresno County Board of Supervisors to represent District 1 in California. He was on the ballot in the general election on November 3, 2026.

## Biography
Mike Karbassi was born in Fresno, California. He earned a bachelor's degree from California State University, Fresno. His career experience includes working as a small businessman. Karbassi has been also affiliated with the Fresno Rotary Club.[1]

# On the Board of Supervisors, MIKE KARBASSI will...
## KEEP FRESNO COUNTY COMMUNITIES SAFE
On the Fresno City Council, Mike Karbassi fought to deliver a historic 900 police officers and 300 firefighters to the force. As our Supervisor, he’ll continue his pledge to only vote for budgets that maintain or add public safety personnel to reduce response times and keep our communities safe.
## CONTINUE TO REDUCE HOMELESSNESS IN OUR COMMUNITIES
Mike Karbassi led the charge to clean up Fresno’s streets and worked to reduce homelessness by more than 25 percent since taking office in 2019. On the Board of Supervisors, he’ll continue to deploy more resources to the westside to get the homeless off our streets and into housing and treatment.
## INVEST IN OUR NEIGHBORHOODS
Mike Karbassi believes that no neighborhood should be left behind. That’s why he’s committed to building new workforce and affordable housing, combating illegal roadside dumping, improving roads, delivering safe routes to schools and investing in parks and trails.

The best leaders are ones who listen. As our Supervisor, Mike will listen and fight to strengthen the communities of western Fresno County.

### 2024
#### Ballotpedia survey responses

Mike Karbassi completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2024. The survey questions appear in bold and are followed by Karbassi's responses.
Expand All
Who are you? Tell us about yourself.
Born and raised in northwest Fresno, I attended local public schools and graduated from Fresno State having majored in business management. My family started a small retail business in northwest Fresno over 42 years ago. My roots in our community run deep.
I ran for City Council in 2019 because I wanted to ensure that our local representative took our neighborhood issues to heart. For too long we weren’t getting our fair share. Our residents work hard and contribute a lot to our city. It wasn’t unreasonable to get want our hard earned tax dollars reinvested in our neighborhoods.
I have spend nearly five years reinvesting million back into NW Fresno. The completed Veterans Blvd overpass has led to reduced commute times and less congestion. I will continue the focus on upgrading traffic signals and crosswalks around our schools to protect our most treasured resource - our kids.
Speaking of safety, I have kept the promise of my “No New Cops, No Budget” pledge. Thats why in the last five years, we have funded 163 NEW Firefighters and Police Officers to keep our homes and businesses safer. That’s led to the dramatic reduction in violent crime in Fresno. In 2023 alone, homicides are down 43%, commercial burglaries down 44%, and home burglaries down 25%, to name a few.
Our work isn’t done yet. We must now focus on nonviolent crimes. Our work on combatting street racing has been successful. We need to continue to go after red light runners and distracted drivers.
Please list below 3 key messages of your campaign. What are the main points you want voters to remember about your goals for your time in office?
- DELIVERED RECORD NUMBER OF COPS & FIREFIGHTERS
- KEPT OUR ROADS SAFE FOR FRESNO FAMILIES
- IMPROVED NW FRESNO ONE BLOCK AT-A-TIME
What areas of public policy are you personally passionate about?
Focus areas include Transportation and Infrastructure, Public Safety, High-Value Job Creation through economic development, and Housing, to name a few.
What qualities do you possess that you believe would make you a successful officeholder?
Having been the incumbent and serving our northwest community for nearly five years, I am the only candidate with real experience and a proven record. I set specific goals during the initial campaign in 2019, promising to reduce crime by hiring more police officers and firefighters, fund a new traffic signal to slow down traffic on Audubon Drive, upgrade the traffic signal in front of Starr Elementary at Sierra and West, and complete Veterans Blvd. All those things have been done and are in progress . In short: Promises Made, Promises Kept. I’ve demonstrated success and would like to continue working with my northwest Fresno neighbors to continue our progress.
What was your very first job? How long did you have it?
My first job as was working in the family business. I was three years old and it was my job to greet all the customers. I was very committed to that. But my first job in adulthood was an internship with Gottschalks through Fresno State’s business internship program. I was very fortunate to have this opportunity to learn and grow.
What is your favorite book? Why?
That’s a tough one. I like historical fiction like The Day of the Jackal by Frederick Foresyth. Thirteen Days by Robert F. Kennedy comes to mind. It’s a good account of the Cuban Missile Crises in 1962. The lesson I learned is that when you feel that your back is to the wall, don’t despair. Rely on the people you can trust. Don’t be afraid to think outside the box and expand your options. You don’t have to only do what is expected and be boxed in. Don’t be afraid to do what is right to do your job.
If you could be any fictional character, who would you want to be?
Jack McCoy from Law and Order. The two who I’d like to meet are Josiah Barlet and Josh Lyman.
What kind of skills or expertise do you believe would be the most helpful for the holders of this office to possess?
Non-governmental experience is really important. We need more elected officials to understand how the real world works beyond government. While there’s a lot local government can do to help residents, I also believe that government isn’t the “go to” answer for every problem. There are times it can make things worse. Having private sector, small business experience has given me a broader perspective. We must approach problems in a way that ensures “the cure isn’t worse than the disease”. My small business experience helps me to do just that.
Tell us your favorite joke.
All the dad jokes out there. I’m known for that.
What organizations or individuals have endorsed your campaign?
Fresno County Sheriff John Zanoni, Sheriff Margaret Mims (ret.), DA Lisa Smittcamp, Mayor Jerry Dyer, Fresno Firefighters Local 202, Fresno Chamber of Commerce, Fresno City Employees Association, Fresno Building and Construction Trades Council, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Local 100,

#### Campaign website
O'Brien's campaign website stated the following:
# As your next Superintendent of Schools, I intend to prioritize the following 3 GOALS:
## GOAL #1: 3rd Grade Literacy
FACT: In Fresno County, 60% of third graders on average are not meeting reading standards. That means that in a class of 25 students, 15 are not meeting literacy standards.
Why Reading Matters
Reading is not merely a skill—it is the foundation upon which all other academic competencies are built, including mathematical reasoning, scientific inquiry, and critical thinking. By empowering students to have strong literacy skills from an early age, we will pave the way for success in every academic discipline and prepare them to navigate the complexities of the modern world.
​
How reading confidence affects our students
A focus on reading will not only elevate our county’s literacy rates but it will also allow us to tackle a variety of interconnected challenges faced by students.
- When our children acquire strong reading skills, it will nurture their self-esteem and confidence, providing them with the tools to express themselves effectively and navigate their academic journeys with assurance.
- Furthermore, by improving literacy, we can alleviate anxiety and frustration often stemming from academic struggles, fostering a more positive school environment.
- Equipped with better reading proficiency, our students will more likely engage in classroom activities, exhibit better behavior, and form stronger connections with peers and teachers.
My response
As part of my educational agenda, I will develop a comprehensive multi-year literacy plan in collaboration with our educational team to address this priority effectively. I am witnessing an exciting return to the “Back to Basics” science of reading approach that I successfully used for twenty years in my own classrooms. I hope to champion this and other proven methods in the development of our county's plan to achieve significant results for the students in our schools.
​
With this plan, we will be taking a foundational step toward enabling Fresno County’s youth to flourish both academically and personally.
## GOAL #2: Partner with Parents and Families!
Why is this important in education?
Parents play an essential role as the first and primary educators in their children's critical early years. As a parent myself, I appreciated having access to information that helped me support my children at school. At the same time, as a teacher and administrator, I saw the impact of strong school to home relationships. In short, our students achieve higher outcomes when they are supported by school and family communities sharing a common vision.
What I know works…
- Providing parents with the necessary support and knowledge around early childhood educational milestones
- Engaging parents in opportunities to learn how to help their children navigate social, emotional and academic challenges as they matriculate through the system
- Partnering with local parenting groups such as Fresno State's Parent University to create modules focused on topics of interest
- Fostering relationships with local community groups to help support family to school connections
What’s my plan?
I aim to collaborate with District leaders and community organizations specializing in parent engagement programs to help parents actively engage in their children's education. ​
​
If we partner with parents and families to support their children, we will be able to strengthen the bridge between home and school, ensuring a more cohesive and collaborative approach to education.
## GOAL #3: Let's Increase our Return on Investment in Education
What I know…
Fresno County receives significant federal and state dollars for TK-12 education totaling in the billions. Yet, our students continue to struggle, with 56% not meeting standards in English Language Arts and 68% not meeting standards in Math in 2023-24.
Why is this?
Simply put, our current approach isn’t working. My experiences in both Clovis and Central Unified have taught me that we must have the courage to change course when our students are not achieving the results they deserve.
​
The answer?
There are teachers all over our county whose students are achieving great results! We need to work together to collaborate on systems and programs that are yielding positive outcomes on a consistent basis. Only through listening to each other, supporting our teachers, and identifying the most effective programs and methodologies, will we begin to move the needle on student achievement.
​
Therefore in Fresno County, I aim to work alongside districts to explore proven approaches so that our significant investment in education returns the results we all need for our kids.
— Eimear O'Brien's campaign website (May 12, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Pacheco's campaign website stated the following:
MARIA'S PLAN TO DELIVER FOR WEST FRESNO COUNTY
## Priorities
# Reduce Costs and Expand Housing
-Streamline permitting and reduce fees for ADUs, modular, and innovative housing to quickly increase supply in rural communities.
-Invest in water and sewer infrastructure to unlock affordable multi-family housing in underserved areas.
-Protect rural renters and mobile home residents by creating fair, local mediation to prevent displacement.
# Create Opportunity
-Bring services directly to rural communities through mobile resource hubs with job support, social services, and mental health care.
-Launch a workforce program that connects people experiencing homelessness to paid public works jobs and pathways to stable housing.
-Partner with Fresno State and local agricultural leaders to create job training in ag-tech and climate-resilient farming.

MARIA'S PLAN TO DELIVER FOR WEST FRESNO COUNTY
## Priorities
# Reduce Costs and Expand Housing
-Streamline permitting and reduce fees for ADUs, modular, and innovative housing to quickly increase supply in rural communities.
-Invest in water and sewer infrastructure to unlock affordable multi-family housing in underserved areas.

-Work together with state leaders and agencies to protect residents from harassment and threats, including transnational repression.
-Create a secure, multilingual reporting system so residents feel safe to report concerns without fear.
-Support community organizations that educate families about their rights and access to resources.

Mike Karbassi is a member of the Fresno City Council in California, representing District 2. He assumed office in 2019. His current term ends on January 2, 2029.
Karbassi ran for election to the Fresno County Board of Supervisors to represent District 1 in California. He was on the ballot in the general election on November 3, 2026.

## Biography
Mike Karbassi was born in Fresno, California. He earned a bachelor's degree from California State University, Fresno. His career experience includes working as a small businessman. Karbassi has been also affiliated with the Fresno Rotary Club.[1]

# On the Board of Supervisors, MIKE KARBASSI will...
## KEEP FRESNO COUNTY COMMUNITIES SAFE
On the Fresno City Council, Mike Karbassi fought to deliver a historic 900 police officers and 300 firefighters to the force. As our Supervisor, he’ll continue his pledge to only vote for budgets that maintain or add public safety personnel to reduce response times and keep our communities safe.
## CONTINUE TO REDUCE HOMELESSNESS IN OUR COMMUNITIES
Mike Karbassi led the charge to clean up Fresno’s streets and worked to reduce homelessness by more than 25 percent since taking office in 2019. On the Board of Supervisors, he’ll continue to deploy more resources to the westside to get the homeless off our streets and into housing and treatment.
## INVEST IN OUR NEIGHBORHOODS
Mike Karbassi believes that no neighborhood should be left behind. That’s why he’s committed to building new workforce and affordable housing, combating illegal roadside dumping, improving roads, delivering safe routes to schools and investing in parks and trails.
## BE THE VOICE OF THE WESTSIDE ON THE BOARD
The best leaders are ones who listen. As our Supervisor, Mike will listen and fight to strengthen the communities of western Fresno County.

### 2024
#### Ballotpedia survey responses
See also: Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection
Mike Karbassi completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2024. The survey questions appear in bold and are followed by Karbassi's responses.
Expand All
Who are you? Tell us about yourself.
Born and raised in northwest Fresno, I attended local public schools and graduated from Fresno State having majored in business management. My family started a small retail business in northwest Fresno over 42 years ago. My roots in our community run deep.
I ran for City Council in 2019 because I wanted to ensure that our local representative took our neighborhood issues to heart. For too long we weren’t getting our fair share. Our residents work hard and contribute a lot to our city. It wasn’t unreasonable to get want our hard earned tax dollars reinvested in our neighborhoods.
I have spend nearly five years reinvesting million back into NW Fresno. The completed Veterans Blvd overpass has led to reduced commute times and less congestion. I will continue the focus on upgrading traffic signals and crosswalks around our schools to protect our most treasured resource - our kids.
Speaking of safety, I have kept the promise of my “No New Cops, No Budget” pledge. Thats why in the last five years, we have funded 163 NEW Firefighters and Police Officers to keep our homes and businesses safer. That’s led to the dramatic reduction in violent crime in Fresno. In 2023 alone, homicides are down 43%, commercial burglaries down 44%, and home burglaries down 25%, to name a few.
Our work isn’t done yet. We must now focus on nonviolent crimes. Our work on combatting street racing has been successful. We need to continue to go after red light runners and distracted drivers.
Please list below 3 key messages of your campaign. What are the main points you want voters to remember about your goals for your time in office?
- DELIVERED RECORD NUMBER OF COPS & FIREFIGHTERS
- KEPT OUR ROADS SAFE FOR FRESNO FAMILIES
- IMPROVED NW FRESNO ONE BLOCK AT-A-TIME
What areas of public policy are you personally passionate about?
Focus areas include Transportation and Infrastructure, Public Safety, High-Value Job Creation through economic development, and Housing, to name a few.
What qualities do you possess that you believe would make you a successful officeholder?
Having been the incumbent and serving our northwest community for nearly five years, I am the only candidate with real experience and a proven record. I set specific goals during the initial campaign in 2019, promising to reduce crime by hiring more police officers and firefighters, fund a new traffic signal to slow down traffic on Audubon Drive, upgrade the traffic signal in front of Starr Elementary at Sierra and West, and complete Veterans Blvd. All those things have been done and are in progress . In short: Promises Made, Promises Kept. I’ve demonstrated success and would like to continue working with my northwest Fresno neighbors to continue our progress.
What was your very first job? How long did you have it?
My first job as was working in the family business. I was three years old and it was my job to greet all the customers. I was very committed to that. But my first job in adulthood was an internship with Gottschalks through Fresno State’s business internship program. I was very fortunate to have this opportunity to learn and grow.
What is your favorite book? Why?
That’s a tough one. I like historical fiction like The Day of the Jackal by Frederick Foresyth. Thirteen Days by Robert F. Kennedy comes to mind. It’s a good account of the Cuban Missile Crises in 1962. The lesson I learned is that when you feel that your back is to the wall, don’t despair. Rely on the people you can trust. Don’t be afraid to think outside the box and expand your options. You don’t have to only do what is expected and be boxed in. Don’t be afraid to do what is right to do your job.
If you could be any fictional character, who would you want to be?
Jack McCoy from Law and Order. The two who I’d like to meet are Josiah Barlet and Josh Lyman.
What kind of skills or expertise do you believe would be the most helpful for the holders of this office to possess?
Non-governmental experience is really important. We need more elected officials to understand how the real world works beyond government. While there’s a lot local government can do to help residents, I also believe that government isn’t the “go to” answer for every problem. There are times it can make things worse. Having private sector, small business experience has given me a broader perspective. We must approach problems in a way that ensures “the cure isn’t worse than the disease”. My small business experience helps me to do just that.
Tell us your favorite joke.
All the dad jokes out there. I’m known for that.
What organizations or individuals have endorsed your campaign?
Fresno County Sheriff John Zanoni, Sheriff Margaret Mims (ret.), DA Lisa Smittcamp, Mayor Jerry Dyer, Fresno Firefighters Local 202, Fresno Chamber of Commerce, Fresno City Employees Association, Fresno Building and Construction Trades Council, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Local 100,

Ballotpedia does not edit or correct typographical errors unless the candidate's campaign requests it.

# Experienced leadership rooted in resilience and real results!
Mayor Pacheco is running to ensure our community in Fresno County has safe neighborhoods, experienced leadership that puts people first, and someone who understands the importance of family values.

## Meet Maria Pacheco
Maria Pacheco is a proven leader who has made public safety a top priority. As Mayor of Kerman, Maria has worked to secure millions of dollars for public safety, support law enforcement and first responders, and invest in safer neighborhoods and infrastructure. She understands that families, businesses, and communities can only thrive when people feel safe.
Maria brings both experience and a personal understanding of the families she serves. The daughter of farmworkers, a wife and mother of six, and Mayor of Kerman, Maria knows the value of hard work, family, and opportunity. She has dedicated her career to public service, education, and strengthening communities across Western Fresno County.
As Mayor, Maria has delivered results—securing investments for public safety and parks, expanding workforce and educational opportunities, and building partnerships across communities to get things done.
Now Maria is running for Fresno County Supervisor to bring that same experienced, hands-on leadership to the county—keeping our communities safe, strengthening our economy, improving roads and infrastructure, expanding access to housing and opportunity, and making sure Western Fresno County families have a strong voice at the County.
Learn More →

Maria’s Plan to Deliver for West Fresno County
## Priorities
### Keep Our Communities Safe
- Put more deputies on the streets and fight for the resources law enforcement needs to respond quickly and keep our community and families safe.
- Strengthen fire and emergency response, particularly in rural communities where response times can be longer.
- Expand crisis-response teams so trained professionals can handle appropriate mental-health calls and allow deputies to focus on serious crime.
- Invest in prevention and youth programs that provide after-school activities, mentorship, job training, and alternatives to gangs and crime.
### Grow Our Local Economy & Create Good Jobs
- Bring more county resources directly to West Fresno County to help small businesses grow and create local jobs.
- Expand workforce training and apprenticeships in agriculture, construction, health care, skilled trades, and emerging industries.
- Partner with Fresno State, community colleges, employers, and labor to connect residents with training for good-paying careers.
- Invest in roads, water, broadband, and infrastructure that attract businesses and allow rural communities to compete for new investment.
### Make Housing More Affordable
- Cut unnecessary delays and streamline permitting for starter homes, ADUs, modular housing, and other affordable housing options.
- Invest in water and sewer infrastructure so communities can build the housing working families need.
- Protect renters, seniors, and mobile-home residents from displacement while expanding the overall housing supply.
- Promote pathways to homeownership so more working families can build financial security and put down roots in West Fresno County.
### Protect Farming, Water & Farm Jobs
- Fight for a reliable water supply for farmers, farmworkers, families, and rural communities.
- Protect agriculture from policies that threaten local farms and jobs and make sure West Fresno County has a strong voice in county and state decisions.
- Support family farms and agricultural businesses by improving infrastructure and cutting unnecessary red tape.
- Prepare the next generation for agriculture by expanding training in ag-tech, water management, equipment, and other modern agricultural careers.

## Campaign themes
#### Ballotpedia survey responses
See also: Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection
Mason L. Magsig completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2026. The survey questions appear in bold and are followed by Magsig's responses.
Expand All
Who are you? Tell us about yourself.
As a lifelong Clovis native, I know that this community cares – it cares about clean streets, safe neighborhoods, and beautiful parks. I'm running to preserve the Clovis Way of Life by ensuring District 1 and Old Town Clovis have the resources needed to keep our community vibrant each and every day, from repairing roads to protecting our neighborhoods.​
Please list below 3 key messages of your campaign. What are the main points you want voters to remember about your goals for your time in office?
- Bring more businesses into the city of Clovis to increase tax revenue to offset costs and increase funding for public safety and infrastructure.
- Maintain 1 officer per 1,000 residents and equip our public safety officers with what they need to succeed.
- Revitalize older neighborhoods by creating street lights where not currently had, maintaining sidewalks, enforcing code enforcement, etc.
What areas of public policy are you personally passionate about?
Zoning, public safety
What organizations or individuals have endorsed your campaign?
Nathan Magsig (County Supervisor)
- Garry Bredefeld (County Supervisor) - David Tangipa (State Assembly) - Diane Pearce (Mayor Pro Tem) - Matt Basgall (Councilmember) - Drew Bessinger (Councilmember) - Mike Karbassi (Councilmember) - Jose Florez (Fmr Mayor) - Clovis Firefighters Assoc - Clovis police officers association - Sheriff Zanoni (Sherrif)
- Clovis Public Safety Employees Association (CPSEA)

#### Campaign website
Wilson's campaign website stated the following:
# Campaign Focus:
- Strengthening public safety by working collaboratively with first responders, law-enforcement and community groups to ensure our neighborhoods and city are safe for everyone.
- Investing in infrastructure by prioritizing the repair of our roads, improvement in public works, and ensuring our local utilities are reliable, resilient, and secure.
- Promoting transparent and responsible management of your hard earned tax dollars to maximum efficiency of our public services without putting undue burdens on our families. I believe that efficient and effective government starts with open communication.
As your councilmember, I will maintain an open-door policy, hosting regular town halls, and community listening sessions to ensure your voices from District 4 are heard to shape our cities policies. Together we can build a stronger, more vibrant and prosperous Clovis City.
I humbly ask for your support, your vote and your partnership for the Clovis Way of Life. Vote Brian Wilson your choice candidate for District 4 Clovis City Council!
— Brian Wilson's campaign website (September 27, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Wilson's campaign website stated the following:
# Campaign Focus:
- Strengthening public safety by working collaboratively with first responders, law-enforcement and community groups to ensure our neighborhoods and city are safe for everyone.
- Investing in infrastructure by prioritizing the repair of our roads, improvement in public works, and ensuring our local utilities are reliable, resilient, and secure.
- Promoting transparent and responsible management of your hard earned tax dollars to maximum efficiency of our public services without putting undue burdens on our families. I believe that efficient and effective government starts with open communication.
As your councilmember, I will maintain an open-door policy, hosting regular town halls, and community listening sessions to ensure your voices from District 4 are heard to shape our cities policies. Together we can build a stronger, more vibrant and prosperous Clovis City.
I humbly ask for your support, your vote and your partnership for the Clovis Way of Life. Vote Brian Wilson your choice candidate for District 4 Clovis City Council!
— Brian Wilson's campaign website (September 27, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Haus' campaign website stated the following:
## Priorities
# What I hear at the door in District 5
### 01
## Your tax dollars, watched closely
Money approved for one purpose has a way of drifting toward another once the vote is over. I do this work now as Co-Chair of the Measure Y Oversight Committee, and I'll keep doing it from the dais.
### 02
## Growth that pays for itself
Clovis is one of the fastest-growing cities in California. New rooftops arrive faster than the roads, water capacity, and staffing that serve them. Development should carry its own infrastructure costs instead of pushing them onto the neighbors who are already here.
### 03
## Neighborhoods that stay safe
As a mother, public safety isn't abstract to me. Clovis is growing quickly and our police and fire staffing has to grow with it — which means funding those positions properly and making sure the people doing the job have real support behind them. That is a budget question as much as a policing one. I'll push for Measure Y dollars to reach front-line staffing, and for open, honest conversations from the dais with the staff who actually do the work.
— Des Haus' campaign website (September 26, 2026)

## Campaign themes
#### Ballotpedia survey responses

Sarah Almond completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2026. The survey questions appear in bold and are followed by Almond's responses.
Expand All
Who are you? Tell us about yourself.
I grew up as a Girl Scout; my mother was my troop leader and believed in community service, and I carried that forward by raising two Girl Scouts of my own. Nineteen years ago, my husband and I packed up our family in St. Louis, Missouri, and moved to Clovis when he was offered a job in the Central Valley. This is where we put down roots, built our village, and made our home. Over the years, I have built a career across healthcare, customer service, and human resources. I worked at Girl Scouts of Central California South, where I was part of the Product Program Team running the Girl Scout Cookie Program; today, I work as a paraprofessional in Clovis Unified's Braille Transcribers' office. My husband and I also co-own a small solar sales company. Every chapter of my life here has deepened my connection to this community and my commitment to serving it. I am not a politician; I am your neighbor, and I want to be your voice.
Please list below 3 key messages of your campaign. What are the main points you want voters to remember about your goals for your time in office?
- Affordable housing: planning that works for both current residents and welcomes young professionals & working families.
- Transportation: our roads and our bus system need to be user-friendly and support the people who live and work in Clovis.
- Accountability around Flock cameras: surveillance technology is being used in ways that raise serious civil liberties concerns, and residents deserve transparency.
What areas of public policy are you personally passionate about?
I’m especially passionate about equal rights and ensuring everyone has a fair opportunity to succeed, regardless of background or circumstances. I support policies that promote fairness, protect people from discrimination, and ensure everyone is treated with dignity and respect.
What organizations or individuals have endorsed your campaign?
Fresno County Democratic Women's Club, Fresno Stonewall Democrats, Fresno County Democratic Party, Clovis Democrats

#### Campaign website
Almond's campaign website stated the following:
# Issues I Want to Address for You
The biggest challenge that we are currently facing in Clovis is "low-income" versus "affordable" housing. Many people are framing our current, mandated housing requirement as a need for “low income" housing, but what Clovis actually needs is housing that is affordable-affordable for young adults and working families. It has become very difficult for college students and new graduates to afford to live independently. These are young professionals who want to move to or come back home to Clovis. We also need to draw working families to Clovis. That will only happen if we provide affordable housing options. Many families are working very hard to be able to put their children into Clovis schools. The “Clovis Way of Life” should be attainable for anyone who wants to share it.
Many current residents are wary of new development in or next to their existing neighborhoods. That should be respected. New development should enhance existing communities and not interfere with them. Neighborhood safety is paramount when planning for future development and continued positive growth. Understanding increased traffic volume and its effect on the condition and maintenance of our roadways, pedestrian trails and bike routes are essential to the continued safety of our community.
Many Clovis residents have voiced their concern about transportation. Our community wants and deserves safer roads, less traffic congestion, and a more robust, user-friendly public transit system. Measure C has been essential in funding many of the recent projects but is expiring in 2027. The state has stepped in, and the replacement, Measure S, Better Roads, Safe Streets, will be in the hands of the voters this November. We need to use these funds to continue improvements to our streets, public transit system, and trails.
As your City Council District 5 Representative, I will be your ear, your voice, and your workhorse to ensure that Clovis remains a safe, thriving, and desirable place to call home. As a Clovis resident, just like you, I want our community to be a place where everyone is proud to call home.
— Sarah Almond's campaign website (September 26, 2026)

New development should enhance existing communities and not interfere with them. Neighborhood safety is paramount when planning for future development and continued positive growth. Understanding increased traffic volume and its effect on the condition and maintenance of our roadways, pedestrian trails and bike routes are essential to the continued safety of our community.
Many Clovis residents have voiced their concern about transportation. Our community wants and deserves safer roads, less traffic congestion, and a more robust, user-friendly public transit system. Measure C has been essential in funding many of the recent projects but is expiring in 2027. The state has stepped in, and the replacement, Measure S, Better Roads, Safe Streets, will be in the hands of the voters this November. We need to use these funds to continue improvements to our streets, public transit system, and trails.
As your City Council District 5 Representative, I will be your ear, your voice, and your workhorse to ensure that Clovis remains a safe, thriving, and desirable place to call home. As a Clovis resident, just like you, I want our community to be a place where everyone is proud to call home.
— Sarah Almond's campaign website (September 26, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Bessinger's campaign website stated the following:
Issues & Priorities
# Where Drew stands.
Real priorities for real families. Here's what Drew is fighting for on the City Council.
## Public Safety
Drew's experience of over 40 years in law enforcement gives him the insight needed to understand the challenges our police and fire personnel face as they work to protect Clovis.
- Fully fund first responders
- Support neighborhood policing
- Invest in emergency preparedness
## Responsible Leadership
Local government should be transparent, accountable, and careful with taxpayer dollars. Drew believes that common sense governance is one of the reasons Clovis has been successful. While Drew will speak about national and state topics publicly, he will avoid bringing these issues into the Council Chambers whenever possible unless there is a direct link to a Clovis-specific issue. Our focus should be on public safety, good roads, clean parks and trails, and all the other things our citizens expect their local government to do.
Sometimes, your Council will have to make decisions that you don't agree with. I understand that, and when I have to make a decision that is controversial I will explain why I am making that decision. You may end up a little mad at me but you will always understand why I felt the need to vote in the manner I did. That's an element in Lincoln's "public opinion bath."
There may be times when Drew and the Council need to make unpopular decisions, possibly very unpopular decisions, but Drew will always explain why that decision needs to be made or not be made. There may be times, and there have been several over the last 9 years, when Drew was the 1-4 vote on an issue he believed in or seriously doubted and he could not vote in favor of. Abraham Lincoln called these moments "public opinion baths."
- Transparent budgets and clear priorities
- Fiscal responsibility, no waste
- Open communication with residents
## Local Businesses
Small businesses are the heart of our city. Having small businesses and larger ones we can get the mix of goods and services we all want. Drew will cut red tape whenever possible, recruit out of town businesses, and help entrepreneurs open, grow, and hire right here at home. Drew will support businesses, big and small, and work to make it easier for them to open and stay open. As Mayor during the first year of COVID, Drew worked hard to reopen Clovis and lobbied State officials, including the Governor, to ease the restrictions placed on small businesses while allowing big businesses to stay open.
We need to advocate for and protect our local businesses from the long-arm of Sacramento that overlooks local small businesses and favors larger national businesses that donate large amounts to some State elected officials at the expense of local businesses and their local employees ... our neighbors!
## Community & Families
From parks to neighborhood events, Drew is committed to a city that brings people together and where families can put down roots for generations. That means working to strengthen our older neighborhoods so young families will be able to buy their first homes and grow with our community. We need to make “the Clovis Way of Life” affordable for our children and later generations too.
- Strengthen older neighborhoods
- Keep the Clovis Way of Life affordable
- Invest in youth programs
- Support seniors and veterans
## Quality of Life
Clean streets, well-kept parks and trails, and reliable services aren't extras — they're the foundation of a great city. Drew will push to add additional trails in our older neighborhoods in SW Clovis, and he understands that quality of life begins with a safe community.
- Well-kept parks and trails
- Additional trails in SW Clovis' older neighborhoods
- Cleaner, safer streets
- Reliable core city services
## Responsible Growth
Our city is growing — and growth must be planned, thoughtful, and true to who we are. District 5 will be the next growth area of Clovis. The “Heritage Grove” planned area will bring mixed types of housing, commercial growth, and trails and parks. We need to ensure we have planned and common-sense growth that strengthens neighborhoods, not overwhelms them.
- Planned, common-sense growth in District 5
- Support the Heritage Grove planned area
- Mixed housing, commercial, trails and parks
- Modernize infrastructure
— Drew Bessinger's campaign website (September 27, 2026)

Who are you? Tell us about yourself.
I grew up as a Girl Scout; my mother was my troop leader and believed in community service, and I carried that forward by raising two Girl Scouts of my own. Nineteen years ago, my husband and I packed up our family in St. Louis, Missouri, and moved to Clovis when he was offered a job in the Central Valley. This is where we put down roots, built our village, and made our home. Over the years, I have built a career across healthcare, customer service, and human resources. I worked at Girl Scouts of Central California South, where I was part of the Product Program Team running the Girl Scout Cookie Program; today, I work as a paraprofessional in Clovis Unified's Braille Transcribers' office. My husband and I also co-own a small solar sales company. Every chapter of my life here has deepened my connection to this community and my commitment to serving it. I am not a politician; I am your neighbor, and I want to be your voice.
Please list below 3 key messages of your campaign. What are the main points you want voters to remember about your goals for your time in office?
- Affordable housing: planning that works for both current residents and welcomes young professionals & working families.

What areas of public policy are you personally passionate about?

What organizations or individuals have endorsed your campaign?
Fresno County Democratic Women's Club, Fresno Stonewall Democrats, Fresno County Democratic Party, Clovis Democrats

#### Campaign website
Bessinger's campaign website stated the following:
Issues & Priorities
# Where Drew stands.
Real priorities for real families. Here's what Drew is fighting for on the City Council.
## Public Safety
Drew's experience of over 40 years in law enforcement gives him the insight needed to understand the challenges our police and fire personnel face as they work to protect Clovis.
- Fully fund first responders
- Support neighborhood policing
- Invest in emergency preparedness
## Responsible Leadership
Local government should be transparent, accountable, and careful with taxpayer dollars. Drew believes that common sense governance is one of the reasons Clovis has been successful. While Drew will speak about national and state topics publicly, he will avoid bringing these issues into the Council Chambers whenever possible unless there is a direct link to a Clovis-specific issue. Our focus should be on public safety, good roads, clean parks and trails, and all the other things our citizens expect their local government to do.
Sometimes, your Council will have to make decisions that you don't agree with. I understand that, and when I have to make a decision that is controversial I will explain why I am making that decision. You may end up a little mad at me but you will always understand why I felt the need to vote in the manner I did. That's an element in Lincoln's "public opinion bath."
There may be times when Drew and the Council need to make unpopular decisions, possibly very unpopular decisions, but Drew will always explain why that decision needs to be made or not be made. There may be times, and there have been several over the last 9 years, when Drew was the 1-4 vote on an issue he believed in or seriously doubted and he could not vote in favor of. Abraham Lincoln called these moments "public opinion baths."
- Transparent budgets and clear priorities
- Fiscal responsibility, no waste
- Open communication with residents
## Local Businesses
Small businesses are the heart of our city. Having small businesses and larger ones we can get the mix of goods and services we all want. Drew will cut red tape whenever possible, recruit out of town businesses, and help entrepreneurs open, grow, and hire right here at home. Drew will support businesses, big and small, and work to make it easier for them to open and stay open. As Mayor during the first year of COVID, Drew worked hard to reopen Clovis and lobbied State officials, including the Governor, to ease the restrictions placed on small businesses while allowing big businesses to stay open.
We need to advocate for and protect our local businesses from the long-arm of Sacramento that overlooks local small businesses and favors larger national businesses that donate large amounts to some State elected officials at the expense of local businesses and their local employees ... our neighbors!
## Community & Families
From parks to neighborhood events, Drew is committed to a city that brings people together and where families can put down roots for generations. That means working to strengthen our older neighborhoods so young families will be able to buy their first homes and grow with our community. We need to make “the Clovis Way of Life” affordable for our children and later generations too.
- Strengthen older neighborhoods
- Keep the Clovis Way of Life affordable
- Invest in youth programs
- Support seniors and veterans
## Quality of Life
Clean streets, well-kept parks and trails, and reliable services aren't extras — they're the foundation of a great city. Drew will push to add additional trails in our older neighborhoods in SW Clovis, and he understands that quality of life begins with a safe community.
- Well-kept parks and trails
- Additional trails in SW Clovis' older neighborhoods
- Cleaner, safer streets
- Reliable core city services
## Responsible Growth
Our city is growing — and growth must be planned, thoughtful, and true to who we are. District 5 will be the next growth area of Clovis. The “Heritage Grove” planned area will bring mixed types of housing, commercial growth, and trails and parks. We need to ensure we have planned and common-sense growth that strengthens neighborhoods, not overwhelms them.
- Planned, common-sense growth in District 5
- Support the Heritage Grove planned area
- Mixed housing, commercial, trails and parks
- Modernize infrastructure
— Drew Bessinger's campaign website (September 27, 2026)

#### Campaign website
Bessinger's campaign website stated the following:
Issues & Priorities
# Where Drew stands.
Real priorities for real families. Here's what Drew is fighting for on the City Council.
## Public Safety
Drew's experience of over 40 years in law enforcement gives him the insight needed to understand the challenges our police and fire personnel face as they work to protect Clovis.
- Fully fund first responders
- Support neighborhood policing
- Invest in emergency preparedness
## Responsible Leadership
Local government should be transparent, accountable, and careful with taxpayer dollars. Drew believes that common sense governance is one of the reasons Clovis has been successful. While Drew will speak about national and state topics publicly, he will avoid bringing these issues into the Council Chambers whenever possible unless there is a direct link to a Clovis-specific issue. Our focus should be on public safety, good roads, clean parks and trails, and all the other things our citizens expect their local government to do.
Sometimes, your Council will have to make decisions that you don't agree with. I understand that, and when I have to make a decision that is controversial I will explain why I am making that decision. You may end up a little mad at me but you will always understand why I felt the need to vote in the manner I did. That's an element in Lincoln's "public opinion bath."
There may be times when Drew and the Council need to make unpopular decisions, possibly very unpopular decisions, but Drew will always explain why that decision needs to be made or not be made. There may be times, and there have been several over the last 9 years, when Drew was the 1-4 vote on an issue he believed in or seriously doubted and he could not vote in favor of. Abraham Lincoln called these moments "public opinion baths."
- Transparent budgets and clear priorities
- Fiscal responsibility, no waste
- Open communication with residents
## Local Businesses
Small businesses are the heart of our city. Having small businesses and larger ones we can get the mix of goods and services we all want. Drew will cut red tape whenever possible, recruit out of town businesses, and help entrepreneurs open, grow, and hire right here at home. Drew will support businesses, big and small, and work to make it easier for them to open and stay open. As Mayor during the first year of COVID, Drew worked hard to reopen Clovis and lobbied State officials, including the Governor, to ease the restrictions placed on small businesses while allowing big businesses to stay open.
We need to advocate for and protect our local businesses from the long-arm of Sacramento that overlooks local small businesses and favors larger national businesses that donate large amounts to some State elected officials at the expense of local businesses and their local employees ... our neighbors!
## Community & Families
From parks to neighborhood events, Drew is committed to a city that brings people together and where families can put down roots for generations. That means working to strengthen our older neighborhoods so young families will be able to buy their first homes and grow with our community. We need to make “the Clovis Way of Life” affordable for our children and later generations too.
- Strengthen older neighborhoods
- Keep the Clovis Way of Life affordable
- Invest in youth programs
- Support seniors and veterans
## Quality of Life
Clean streets, well-kept parks and trails, and reliable services aren't extras — they're the foundation of a great city. Drew will push to add additional trails in our older neighborhoods in SW Clovis, and he understands that quality of life begins with a safe community.
- Well-kept parks and trails
- Additional trails in SW Clovis' older neighborhoods
- Cleaner, safer streets
- Reliable core city services
## Responsible Growth
Our city is growing — and growth must be planned, thoughtful, and true to who we are. District 5 will be the next growth area of Clovis. The “Heritage Grove” planned area will bring mixed types of housing, commercial growth, and trails and parks. We need to ensure we have planned and common-sense growth that strengthens neighborhoods, not overwhelms them.
- Planned, common-sense growth in District 5
- Support the Heritage Grove planned area
- Mixed housing, commercial, trails and parks
- Modernize infrastructure
— Drew Bessinger's campaign website (September 27, 2026)

Naindeep Singh is a member of the Central Unified Board of Trustees in California, representing Trustee Area 7. He assumed office in 2018. His current term ends on December 11, 2026. Singh did not run for re-election to Central Unified School District Board of Trustees Trustee Area 7 in 2026.
Singh ran for election to the Fresno City Council to represent District 1 in California. He was on the ballot in the general election on November 3, 2026.

### “We aren’t running for a seat; we are running to reclaim our city.”
### Meet Naindeep
Naindeep Singh is an educator, nonprofit leader, and Central Unified School Board trustee running for Fresno City Council District 1 with a bold plan to make Fresno affordable for working families. Raised in Fresno, he has overseen a $300 million public school budget, authored statewide legislation to expand bilingual services, stood with workers against wage theft, and built a local organization that has brought millions of dollars into the Valley, creating jobs and opportunity for young people.
Now, as rent and utility bills push families to the edge, Naindeep believes City Hall must fight for everyday people, not insiders. He’ll use every tool available to cap utility hikes, stop unfair rate increases, prevent evictions before they happen, invest in youth workforce pathways, and pass a “Fresno First” policy that keeps public dollars in local hands. Fresno’s working class families are being squeezed, but build a city, together, where working people can stay, thrive, and raise their children with dignity.

Keshia Thomas is a member of the Fresno Unified Board of Education in California, representing Trustee Area 1. She assumed office in 2019. Her current term ends on December 11, 2026. Thomas did not run for re-election to Fresno Unified School District Board of Education Trustee Area 1 in 2026.
Thomas ran for election to the Fresno City Council to represent District 3 in California. She was on the ballot in the general election on November 3, 2026.

Keshia Thomas is a member of the Fresno Unified Board of Education in California, representing Trustee Area 1. She assumed office in 2019. Her current term ends on December 11, 2026. Thomas did not run for re-election to Fresno Unified School District Board of Education Trustee Area 1 in 2026.
Thomas ran for election to the Fresno City Council to represent District 3 in California. She was on the ballot in the general election on November 3, 2026.

# Ariana Martínez Lott
Strong communities aren’t built by City Hall insiders. They’re built by neighbors who show up for one another, and Ariana is running to make sure District 7’s government finally does the same.
Get Involved

Running for District 7
Ariana with her two children. District 7 is the only home they’ve ever known.
Dear Neighbor
“District 7 is the only home my two children have ever known.”
I was born in Madera to farmworker parents and raised as one of six children. When I was 12, my brother was born with Down syndrome, and I learned early that a healthy community means taking the needs of others seriously. I volunteered in his classrooms, then became a substitute teacher myself.
After graduating from Fresno State in 2010, I stayed and got to work: park cleanups, school appreciation events, and fifteen years alongside neighbors organizing for safer streets, better parks, and homes families can actually afford.
Ariana
Read Ariana’s full story
Where Ariana Stands
## Built for the neighborhood, not around it
Right now, elected officials and special interests are rushing a plan to expand Fresno’s limits so developers can build outward: the Southeast Development Area (SEDA). Ariana says invest in the neighborhoods we already call home instead.
No to SEDA
### Protect Our Neighborhoods
- Keep taxpayer dollars out of developers’ pockets
- Protect police, fire, trash and water service from being stretched thin
- Stop utility rates from continuing to skyrocket

- A Residential Response Team for loose dogs and neighborhood theft
- No collaboration between ICE and local law enforcement
- Bring back the City of Fresno Youth Commission
- More parks, more trees, safer streets

- Safe Routes to School: sidewalks and traffic calming
- Summer enrichment aligned to caregivers’ work schedules
- Paid youth internship programs
Affordability
### Housing Every Family Can Afford
- Expand funding and eligibility for home repair programs
- Protect renters from wrongful eviction
- Expand homeownership assistance and mental health support

#### Campaign website
Gurm's campaign website stated the following:
# Nav Gurm's Vision for Fresno.
## Addressing Cost of Living
Fresno families, like mine and yours, are feeling the pinch of rising costs—from inflation and gas prices to housing and utilities. I will fight to ensure that our local utility rates remain affordable and that every city service is cost-effective for our residents.
## Strengthening Public Safety
A safe Fresno is a thriving Fresno. I will work to ensure that our police and fire departments have the resources and personnel they need to protect and serve our neighborhoods.
## Investing in Fresno’s Economy
To build a stronger economy, we need to support the backbone of our city—small businesses—while fostering innovation and recruiting major employers offering career-track jobs
## Parks
Our parks are vital spaces for families, children, and seniors alike. I will launch an annual survey to ensure our parks are clean, accessible, and meeting the needs of every resident.
## Fair Share of Dollars
Fresno deserves its fair share of state and federal funding. I will work tirelessly to bring those dollars home.
## Homelessness
Homelessness requires a compassionate yet practical approach. I will foster partnerships between the city, county, nonprofits, and faith-based organizations to deliver real solutions.
## Infrastructure
Fresno’s roads, sidewalks, and infrastructure need serious attention. I will prioritize fixing potholes, modernizing our transit systems, and ensuring that every neighborhood has access to safe and reliable infrastructure.
## Sports and Entertainment
Sports and entertainment bring communities together and put cities on the map. I’ll work to bring professional soccer to Fresno, support Fresno State’s entry into the PAC-12, and advocate for expanding entertainment venues across the city. Sports can be a catalyst for economic growth and civic pride.
## A Vision for Blackstone and Manchester Mall
Manchester Mall has the potential to become Fresno’s first major mixed-use development—a vibrant space where people can live, work, shop, and play. I will work with developers, investors, and community members to turn this vision into reality, making Blackstone a corridor of opportunity for all.
## Housing
Fresno must address its housing crisis by increasing the supply of all types of housing—affordable units, starter homes, and market-rate apartments. I will streamline approval processes and work with builders to ensure we meet the needs of a growing population without sacrificing quality or sustainability.
## Engaging the Youth
Our city’s future depends on our young people. I will create initiatives to engage youth in decision-making processes, expand mentorship and internship opportunities, and support programs that inspire the next generation of Fresno leaders. Investing in our youth is investing in Fresno’s success.
## Seniors and Veterans
Our seniors and veterans have given so much to our community, and it’s time we give back. I will advocate for expanded senior services, improved healthcare access, and programs that honor and support our veterans. Ensuring dignity and opportunity for these groups is a personal priority for me.
## Constituent Services
Every resident deserves to have their voice heard. I will establish accessible office hours, improve communication channels, and ensure that every concern—big or small—is addressed promptly. My commitment is to serve as an advocate for every person in District 7 – you deserve a response from your Councilmember.
﻿
## Fiscal Responsibility
Fresno’s budget must reflect the priorities of its residents. I will ensure that every dollar spent delivers tangible results, cutting waste and increasing transparency. Fiscal responsibility isn’t just about balancing the budget—it’s about investing in our community’s future.
— Nav Gurm's campaign website (March 27, 2026)
